candidates.title: Map resume facts into application forms

demandEvidence.chore: I spent two hours every day filling my resume data to freshly developed forms made specifically to the hiring process of one or two companies.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I spent two hours every day filling my resume data to freshly developed forms made specifically to the hiring process of one or two companies.

ease.reason: A beginner could map supplied resume facts to a few sample fields; no implementation reference supports live form access.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: job seekers may pay to reduce repetitive application entry; this post shows a chore, not purchase intent.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock can draft values for manually supplied fields; company forms and accuracy remain untested.

autonomy.reason: A draft can be reused, but a person must check every field and submit each form; no automation capability is documented.

evidence.reason: The fresh post states a daily two-hour resume-entry chore for forms tailored to one or two companies, but no fields or corroboration.

candidates.reason: Assessed as a proposed draft of resume facts for manually supplied application fields; no supported live integration. Provisional mean is below threshold.

candidates.title: Summarize orders and pending requests

demandEvidence.chore: Daily reports: Generate summaries of completed orders, cancellations, and pending requests.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: Daily reports: Generate summaries of completed orders, cancellations, and pending requests.

ease.reason: A beginner can summarize operator-supplied sample rows, but no attached reference supports data ingestion or report generation.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: service operators may pay to prepare recurring daily reports; this post establishes no payment or buyer validation.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock can summarize synthetic order, cancellation and pending-request rows; actual data access is unknown.

autonomy.reason: A repeatable summary could be drafted, but a person must verify counts and interpretation; no implementation support is attached.

evidence.reason: The post names daily summaries of completed orders, cancellations and pending requests, but provides no inputs or constraints.

candidates.reason: Assessed a proposed summary from synthetic/operator-supplied rows. Inputs, accuracy and integration are unverified; provisional mean is below threshold.

candidates.title: Draft replies to Messenger customer messages

demandEvidence.chore: I am building a scenario in Make.com to handle customer messages received through Facebook Messenger.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I am building a scenario in Make.com to handle customer messages received through Facebook Messenger.

ease.reason: A beginner can test drafts using sample message text, but no attached reference supports Messenger or reply generation.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: small service firms may pay for reply drafting; this build description does not establish external buyer intent or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock can draft from operator-supplied examples; live access, message types and response quality remain untested.

autonomy.reason: Drafting can repeat, but a person must check context and approve every reply; no implementation reference is supplied.

evidence.reason: The post says a scenario is being built to handle Facebook Messenger customer messages, without volume, exact output or corroboration.

candidates.reason: Assessed only a proposed human-reviewed draft from sample message text. The source is a build description, and prior decisions on this same evidence were below threshold; this reassessment remains below threshold.

rejected.title: Map resume facts into application forms
rejected.reason: Below threshold on this fresh post: the specific daily chore supports a manually supplied field-mapping experiment, but no live form implementation or buyer payment is evidenced.

steps.message: Assessed all nine sealed discussion assignments. Three concrete chores received five provisional criterion ratings and explicit below-threshold decisions; six were excluded for insufficient task evidence or a one-off bug. No post meets the threshold.
